reason: Marisol ran 53 miles when 38 were planned, after weeks of 32, 24, 27 and 37. The draft treats that as the risk it is and answers her question with a direct, honest no. It explains why: feeling fine during a run doesn't mean the body has absorbed the load, and the jump was about 40 percent. Next week drops to about 39 miles (6+8+6+5+14), close to what was planned. The long run comes down from 20 to 14 miles at an easy pace. That is sensible progression and avoids the volume and long-run jump checks. The plan keeps her schedule (Monday and Friday off, the session on Wednesday, the long run on Sunday). Each day has a distance and a heart-rate cap or pace, so it can be run as written. The threshold pace of 8:00/mi is reasonable for a sub-3:45 goal. It says the build resumes gradually and that marathon-pace work waits until the calves settle. The tight calves are tightness, not pain, so keeping a modest three-rep session is acceptable. The draft also limits it with "stop after three." Marks off: the safety flag names a "right knee" that Marisol never mentioned, which may be invented. The draft also doesn't say what to do if the calf tightness turns into pain, such as dropping the quality session or seeing a physio. Otherwise it is a strong, specific, safe reply.

Body: "Calves tight on Sunday night, otherwise great."
Feeling: "Like I've turned a corner."
Asks: "I ran way more than the plan and felt fine. Can I keep this up?"

From the week of Sep 21 the volume builds again gradually, with marathon-pace work in some long runs once the calves feel settled.
